newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria ministry sees change to export inspections.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria ministry sees change to export inspections.

text.p: Nigeria's commerce ministry expects an end to pre-shipment inspections of agricultural produce by two private agencies and a return to checks by government agents, a senior ministry official said on Monday.
"The policy will be changed in the next financial year," the official said.
He said a meeting had recently been held with the finance ministry, which introduced the private agencies in 1996, at which it had been agreed to scrap the policy.

Global Inspection Services and Robinson International Services were appointed to take charge of pre-shipment inspections of both oil and non-oil exports. They took over from the Federal Produce Inspection Service.
The official said he was unable to say whether pre-shipment inspections of oil exports, as well as agricultural produce, would be affected by the change.
"The pre-shipment measure has been a disaster to our export trade. It has left a vacuum in quality control, with quality control now voluntary on the part of commodity exporters," the official said.

At the time the policy was introduced, exporters complained about the imposition of an extra one percent levy, but at the same time said their own checks mattered more than those carried out by either a government or private agency.
Nigeria's principal agricultural export, cocoa, as well as its rubber, have over the years earned a reputation for poor quality and tend to be sold at a discount on the world market.
